turns.t: Good morning, doctor. I have come back about my left leg, as you asked me to when we last met.
Good morning, Mr. Adeyemi. I'm glad you could make it. Please, have a seat and get comfortable. How have you been getting on since then?
Quite well, thank you. A great deal calmer, I must say. I was rather frightened at the time, and my wife was even more so.
That's completely understandable. Take your time here, there's no rush at all. Has the weakness come back at any point since our last visit?
No, not at all. I walked to the mailbox and back twice yesterday, simply to be certain.
I like that, a careful experiment. And what about numbness in the leg or foot?
None, thank you.
Good. Let's go over your medicines so the chart is right. Are you still on the same tablet as before?
Yes, amlodipine, 5 milligrams, once daily, for my high blood pressure. That is the only one.
Thank you. And are there any allergies I should keep on the record?
Codeine. I was allergic to it as a young man. It brought me out in hives, and I have avoided it ever since.
Hives from codeine. I'll make sure that's written clearly. Anything else in your health history besides the blood pressure?
Varicose veins in the right leg. Nothing else of note, I believe.
Perfect. Now let me check a couple of numbers, and then I'd like to test the leg myself.
Of course. Shall I roll up my sleeve?
Please. This will take just a moment.
Blood pressure is 128 over 78, and your pulse is 70. That looks lovely.
I am relieved to hear it. I had a rather large breakfast, I confess, and I wondered whether it would show.
It certainly didn't. Now lie back on the couch for me. I'd like you to push your left foot against my hand, as hard as you can, like pressing a gas pedal.
Like this? I shall do my best.
Excellent. The strength in your left leg is full, and just as strong as the right.
That is a great comfort. May I ask what we do now?
Good question. I don't want to say anything about causes yet, because I'd be guessing. What I'd like to do is arrange an MRI scan of your lower back, so we can look properly.
An MRI. Is that the tube one with the loud knocking?
That's the one. It's noisy but painless, and they'll give you earplugs. Takes about thirty minutes.
I can manage thirty minutes, so long as nobody makes me hurry out.
Nobody will. Tell the radiographer if you feel uneasy, and they'll talk you through it.
Thank you. Will the appointment come by post?
Reception will phone you, and they'll send a letter as well. I'd like to see you again in four weeks to go over the scan together.
Four weeks. That suits me well. My daughter lives a good way off and I should like to visit her afterwards.
That brings up the driving. For long trips, stop every two hours, get out of the car and walk about for a few minutes.
Every two hours. I shall write that on a card for the dashboard.
Perfect. And should anything feel different between now and then, don't wait for the appointment, just phone the clinic.
I will, doctor. Thank you for being so patient with me.
It's a pleasure. Safe travels, Mr. Adeyemi, and give your wife my best.
I shall indeed. Good day to you.
